messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.099 atm) the equilibrium between solid ice I and liquid water lies just below the normal 0 °C freezing point.  
For pure water the melting curve has a positive slope (dP/dT > 0), so lowering the pressure lowers the melting temperature.  

Using the water phase‑diagram (or a fit to the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice I↔water transition) gives:

| Pressure | Freezing / Melting Point |
|----------|---------------------------|
| 1 bar (101.3 kPa) | 0.00 °C |
| 20 kPa | –1.0 °C |
| 10 kPa | **≈ –2.0 °C** |

So the freezing point of *pure* water at 10 kPa is approximately **–2 °C** (more precisely about –1.8 °C to –2.2 °C depending on the reference data set).  

If you need the corresponding boiling point at the same pressure, it’s about 45 °C (you can get a more precise value from the Antoine equation or the tool `thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point`).
